sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header with the date of the maamar.
This section explains that turning to holiness above or to the opposite below is called foolishness and heresy.
This section discusses the Zohar's wonder at how a soul could sin, and the Alter Rebbe's teaching that a Jew cannot truly be separate from G‑dliness.

translations.translation: And as the Zohar says on the verse “And when a soul will sin,”
that the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Torah wonder: how is it possible that “it will sin”?
Even though it refers to Nefesh,
which is the lowest level of the five names of the soul,
and as the Zohar there specifically emphasizes “Nefesh,” and nevertheless it is wondrous.
And known is the saying of the Alter Rebbe: “A Jew—whether he wants to or not—cannot be a separate entity from G‑dliness.”
And only because he does not feel that through a transgression he becomes separate,
and it seems to him that he is still within Judaism,
the 365 negative commandments and all Rabbinic prohibitions,
